messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY -> P2 alert: Missing observability for EosSystems (dedicated-prod-eos-01). Traces/logs not ingested since 2026-03-14T03:10Z. Metrics partially partitioned. Paging on-call. https://pd.example/INC12345

alex.sre: oncall here, grabbing context. which customers/nodes affected?

sam.se: EosSystems — dedicated pool prod-eos-01 in us-east-2. Their model-serving nodes stopped sending spans/logs at ~03:10Z. Prom metrics show some shards missing (p95 spike). Customer is on the call.

priya.runtime: quick check from runtime side: trace ingest endpoint shows 0 spans from that pool after 03:10Z. Forwarder logs show repeated 403 responses from our ingest endpoint. suspect a blocking egress or API key issue.

morgan.platform: deploy-bot: forwarder-edge rollout v1.2.4 completed at 02:49Z to prod-eos-01 nodes. No config changes after that on our side.

alex.sre: ok. two likely root causes: (A) customer network change blocking egress to forwarder IPs, (B) API key mismatch/rotation. Which one has evidence?

priya.runtime: running a health curl against forwarder from one of the edge nodes now:

```
# from an edge node (ssh into 10.1.5.22)
curl -v https://forwarder.redwood.internal/api/health
```

priya.runtime: result: HTTP/2 403 \"api key missing\". headers show request arrives at our edge but rejected at auth layer. That implies node can reach us but key not accepted.

sam.se: customer ops says they rotated keys yesterday via internal automation but only for their internal services, not forwarding keys — they're pretty sure they did not rotate forwarder key. They're on the call to check ACLs.

morgan.platform: checking our network logs: I can see DENY entries in the customer's flow logs for destination 35.172.45.8 from 10.1.5.*/24 starting at 03:10Z — looks like a NAT rule change took out some outbound ranges. so connectivity is intermittent: some nodes hit forwarder, some denied.

alex.sre: combined hypothesis: partial network ACL change + stale key on some nodes (maybe bootstrap race during rotation). Need a mitigation that doesn't require a permanent customer network change. Customer prefers we avoid changing their security groups. they allow a short window for us to touch a bastion.

priya.runtime: mitigation proposal (fast): stand up a transient TLS proxy in the customer's bastion that tunnels node traffic to our forwarder, then update local forwarder config to point at localhost:20000. Steps below — can do as rolling config so no node restarts.

priya.runtime: runbook snippet:

```
# on bastion (one-liner)
ssh -fN -L 20000:forwarder.redwood.internal:443 ec2-user@bastion-prod-eos
# on nodes: set FORWARDER_URL=https://localhost:20000/v1
# or for systemd unit: drop-in with env override and `systemctl reload-or-restart forwarder.service`
```

priya.runtime: alternative: deploy a small sidecar log-bridge container that forwards via an outbound path customer confirms is allowed. but that requires a quick container rollout.

morgan.platform: I can provision the proxy container on the bastion and expose a local port. I have an image ready (redwood-proxy:hotfix).

leah.support: I'll message CS/AE and the customer right now: inform EosSystems we will run a transient proxy and reconfigure nodes to point at localhost. ETA target 40m, will update every 15.

alex.sre: alex starting the proxy setup now. Priya, can you verify ingestion once proxy is up? Morgan, capture relevant flow logs and keep an eye on denied rules.

priya.runtime: will watch traces index and forwarder logs. query: `index:traces AND service:eos*` every minute.

ops-bot: NOTE: autopilot detected high 403 rate from prod-eos-01 to forwarder api-key auth service. Alert suppressed until manual ack.

priya.runtime: proxy is up on bastion (bind 20000 -> forwarder:443). updating node config via rolling agent to point at https://localhost:20000/v1/traces now.

sam.se: customer confirmed they did a NAT change earlier today via IaC template; that removed a /24 our nodes used for outbound. they will revert but estimate 1 hour until full rollout. they prefer proxy until they complete revert.

priya.runtime: first traces are appearing in the index from prod-eos-01 at 03:35Z. tailing forwarder logs: we see auth accepted for proxied requests.

alex.sre: good. mark mitigation in place. action items while we keep proxy:
- ensure proxy is monitored and auto-restarted
- rotate any nodes still using old endpoint
- capture timeline for postmortem

morgan.platform: capturing packet samples and flow logs. saving to /var/logs/incidents/2361112222/ for handoff.

leah.support: notifying EosSystems: initial mitigation succeeded, traces resumed. we're keeping proxy up until they complete NAT rollback. sharing runbook and ETA 60m. they asked for a short postmortem afterwards.

alex.sre: severity P2, customer impact: missing spans and logs for one dedicated pool (prod-eos-01) for ~25m before mitigation. metrics partially impacted for related shards.

alex.sre: handoff to taylor.sre for night coverage at 04:30Z — summary + link to artifact folder in incident ticket: /incidents/2361112222. Taylor, please take over monitoring and customer comms; also follow up on post-incident items (alert for forwarder-403 spike, per-tenant forwarder health metric).

taylor.sre: acked, taking handoff. please leave the proxy configuration and credentials in the ticket (do not post secrets here). will schedule a follow-up with eng-runtime tomorrow for a durable fix.

alex.sre: leaving a short checklist in ticket: who touched bastion, proxy image tag, nodes rolled, start/stop times, customer confirmation.

priya.runtime: post-incident note: we need to add a 'forwarder-acceptance' synthetic check per tenant that validates both reachability and API-key acceptance (403 spikes). will open an RFC/PR.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: P2 -> Mitigated (proxy active). Customer impact: traces/logs missing for 25m prior to mitigation. follow-up required: timeline, alert tuning, durable network guidance for dedicated customers.

leah.support: thanks team. closing the active paging for now; I'll keep the customer looped.

alex.sre: good job everyone :thumbsup:
